key_insight: GRASP learns probabilistic logic programs by combining functional gradient boosting with LLM-guided rule proposal, making symbolic relational structure learning more tractable and interpretable.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical neurosymbolic path for building explainable models in relational scientific domains where exhaustive symbolic search is too expensive.
method: Cast probabilistic logic program learning as functional gradient boosting over weighted first-order rules.
Use an LLM as a proposal oracle to generate candidate rules instead of performing combinatorial inner-loop search.
Aggregate learned rules into an interpretable ensemble that preserves boosting-style learning behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on four relational benchmarks, including Tox21, mutagenesis, and Cora, with improvements over symbolic, neural, and LLM-based baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and reliability of LLM-proposed rules, so invalid or biased proposals could affect learning stability and final rule quality.
paper_title: Learning Probabilistic Logic Programs with Functional Gradient Guided Language Models
